problem: Outdoor mobile robot navigation depends on geographic information systems (GIS), which limits it in complex and changing scenes; prior visual-language navigation methods do not exploit landmark selection and scene memory.
motivation: Removing GIS dependence would allow autonomous outdoor navigation from language instructions alone. The paper's driving idea is to combine language guidance with a memory of landmarks passed along the route, so the agent can localize and match its position and act accordingly.
key_idea: Select landmarks along the route, add prompt guidance, and let the agent use visual-language instructions plus a memory of scene features and passed-by landmarks to navigate without GIS.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations or analysis can be cited. The abstract suggests that landmark selection plus scene memory lets the agent ascertain its position by matching, replacing GIS-based localization.
method: Landmark selection: chooses landmarks the agent passes on the route (details not given in the abstract).
Prompt guidance: adds prompts to the visual-language instruction to guide movement direction.
Scene memory: remembers scene features of passed landmarks; when the agent passes one it matches its position to it and executes the corresponding action.

setting.simulator: not specified (likely outdoor street-view VLN such as Touchdown, unconfirmed)
